title: The Influence of Self-Efficacy, Social Support, and the Use of a Visual Metaphor on the Quality of Life and Psychological Distress of Patients with Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
summary:
Oral cancer is a very common disease, and the number of people affected worldwide is expected to continue rising in the coming years. This diagnosis and the subsequent treatments often have a severe impact on patients' lives. Many suffer from pain or experience difficulties with speaking and swallowing. Changes to facial appearance can also occur. All of this is not only physically, but also emotionally, extremely distressful.

While medicine has made great advances in recent years to improve patient survival rates, psychological support often still lags behind. Although general support services like stress management or behavioral therapy are beneficial, there is a lack of simple, targeted methods that directly empower patients in their everyday lives.

This is where our study comes in: We want to find out to which extent the self-confidence and inner mindset of patients helps them cope with the disease. To do this, we are testing a specific, straightforward method that utilizes images and visualization. We want to investigate whether the patients' inner mindset helps them feel mentally stronger, and whether this consequently improves their quality of life and reduces psychological distress.
conditions: patients with squamosa cell cancer of the mouth

interventions.name:
Subproject A: Cross-Sectional Study
During their inpatient or outpatient stay, eligible patients will be informed about the study and invited to participate on a voluntary basis. Furthermore, the following procedures are to be conducted by the attending physician during this appointment:

General

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity (OSCC).

Capacity to provide informed consent: Participants must possess the cognitive ability to understand the nature, significance, and implications of the study.

Voluntary participation: Submission of a signed written informed consent form, provided without coercion and with the understanding that withdrawal is possible at any time
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to undergo examination due to poor performance status 

Pre-existing psychiatric disorders diagnosed prior to the initial oncological diagnosis:
Pre-existing major depressive disorder (severe).
Schizoaffective disorder
Bipolar affective disorder.
Schizophrenia
